newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week - FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week - FHLMC.

text.p: The average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell in the week ending February 7 from the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
The 30-year interest rate dipped to an average 7.74 percent from 7.88 percent last week, while the 15-year fell to 7.25 percent from 7.38 percent, Freddie Mac said.
One-year adjustable-rate mortgages also inched down to an average 5.51 percent from 5.55 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year 6.51 percent and the ARM 5.33 percent.
"As was expected, the Federal Reserve met Tuesday of this week and did not raise interest rates," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"This news, combined with a low inflation rate, helped keep interest rates low and affordable, which is where we expect them to stay for the near future at least," Van Order added.

On Tuesday the Commerce Department also reported that U.S. December single-family home sales fell one percent to an annualized rate of 783,000 units. But it also said total 1996 sales, at 756,000 units, were the strongest for any year since 1978.
The National Association of Realtors said Monday the Housing Affordability Index rose to 127.0 in the fourth quarter of 1996 from 120.0 in the third quarter.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, down from 1.8 percent last week. They charged 1.7 percent on the 15-year, unchanged from last week, and 1.3 percent on the ARM, down from 1.4 percent the prior week.
